skills.name: Practical preparation: reading a geographical coordinate

note.text: To locate a point, read latitude and longitude from their reference lines and include the hemispheres. This guided practical uses an invented graticule on screen. Start with the parallel through the point, then the meridian. Check the spacing of the labelled lines before estimating an intermediate value. Record the coordinate in your exercise book with latitude first. The practice checks written map reading, not the accuracy of a real field survey.

sections.heading: Understand the ideas
sections.text: To locate a point, read latitude and longitude from their reference lines and include the hemispheres. This guided practical uses an invented graticule on screen. Start with the parallel through the point, then the meridian. Check the spacing of the labelled lines before estimating an intermediate value. Record the coordinate in your exercise book with latitude first. The practice checks written map reading, not the accuracy of a real field survey.

sections.heading: Apply the ideas locally
sections.text: The diagram marks A on an invented grid. All points used here lie north of the Equator and east of Greenwich. Trace A horizontally to the latitude labels, and vertically to the longitude labels. Because each point lies on labelled lines, no estimate is needed in these examples. These coordinates are not being presented as actual locations of named Cameroonian towns.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Write the reference line and hemisphere beside each value. Check that the value you read belongs to the correct axis. For an actual map, consult its key and projection as well. Swapping the two values moves the point and changes its meaning.

key_words.meaning: the north/south angle read from the parallel through a point
the east/west angle read from the meridian through a point
the direction that completes an angular coordinate

examples: A learner follows A's horizontal line to the northward labels.
A learner follows A's vertical line to the eastward labels.
A learner writes north or south after the latitude angle.

mistake.wrong: Read longitude labels to obtain latitude.
mistake.right: latitude reading: the north/south angle read from the parallel through a point.
mistake.why: Use the parallel's latitude label, not the meridian's longitude label.

questions.prompt: Read point A on the graticule. Give its latitude in degrees north.
solution: Read the horizontal parallel through A.

questions.prompt: Read point A on the graticule. Give its longitude in degrees east.
solution: Read the vertical meridian through A.
